title: OpenSUpdater Malware Hides Reflective Loader Inside Recompiled 7-Zip SFX to Evade Detection
content_md: Threat actors are hiding an OpenSUpdater reflective loader inside a recompiled 7-Zip self-extracting archive (SFX) module. The installer contains a genuine foobar2000 setup file, but the malicious code runs from the extraction stub itself a component analysts may overlook when the extracted files appear clean. Recent samples are detected as OpenSUpdater by ESET and Snackarcin by Microsoft. A normal 7-Zip SFX installer combines a decompression stub, a text configuration and an embedded archive. The stub extracts files, writes them to disk and runs a program named in the configuration. An analyst investigating a suspicious installer would therefore have good reason to check that program first. OpenSUpdater Conceals Loader in 7-Zip In the reported samples, that program is a genuine foobar2000 installer named setup.exe . The surrounding package raises questions, however it is signed by Animated Productions, LLC, a purported game-app developer, and its version information contains seemingly random words. Its certificate also contains repeated padding bytes. The padding does not prove what the attacker intended, but the unusual packaging warrants a closer look. Buildup of a 7zip SFX file and its plain text configuration (Source: gdatasoftware) The loader is not hidden in setup.exe or the SFX configuration.
